To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spectral diffusion and resonant intermoleculer energy transfer occur on time scales much shorter than the hydrogen bond lifetime.

the OH stretching vibration of liquid H2 O is characterized by a short time spectral diffusion on a sub-picosecond timescale, which slows down at low temperature, and by a resonant energy transfer on a sub-100 fs time scale, which is unaffected at low temperature.
the two dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectrum of liquid H 2O shows a loss of frequency correlations within 50 fs, which slows down with decreasing temperatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temperature dependence of the OH stretching vibrations of liquid water.
the dynamics of the hydrogen bond in liquid water.
the study of the dynamics of liquid water by two dimensional infrared spectroscopy, a new technique for investigating the dynamics of liquids and solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temperature dependence of the two-dimensional infrared spectrum of liquid water is dominated by spectral diffusion.
the two dimensional infrared measurements show a slowing down of spectral diffusion in the OH stretch with decreasing temperature, while the energy transfer time remains unaffected.
the two dimensional infrared technique provides the first spectroscopic insight into the time scales of the hydrogen bond dynamics in liquid water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the OH stretching vibration of liquid water is a highly delocalized excitation that is coupled to a large number of librational excitations, which are responsible for the loss of frequency correlations.
the OH stretching vibration is a very good probe for structural dynamics of liquid water, which is a result of a large spectral diffusion time and the absence of resonant energy transfer.

the OH stretch vibrations in liquid water are delocalized over several water molecules on the femtosecond time scale, and that the delocalization is affected by the temperature and by the strength of the hydrogen bonds.

, at low temperatures, hydrogen bonds are strong and rigid.
, in the liquid, the hydrogen bonding network of water is not static, but is constantly fluctuating.
